summary: We couldn't confirm Alabama's Medicaid breast pump coverage from an official source. Check with your Medicaid plan.
In Alaska, Medicaid covers manual and electric breast pumps with a prescription and no prior authorization, one of each every three years.
timing_and_limits: Fee schedule maximum of 1 manual (E0602) and 1 electric (E0603) pump per 3 years

summary: In Arizona, AHCCCS covers manual, electric and hospital-grade breast pumps ordered by a doctor or other practitioner.
In Arkansas, Medicaid doesn't pay for breast pumps, which aren't on its list of payable equipment.
In California, Medi-Cal covers manual, electric and hospital-grade breast pumps, and managed care plans can't require prior authorization for manual or electric pumps.
timing_and_limits: Plans are encouraged (not required) to provide a pump at 32 weeks 0 days gestation, or earlier for high-risk pregnancies

summary: In Colorado, Medicaid covers manual and electric breast pumps from 28 weeks of pregnancy with a prescription and no prior authorization.
timing_and_limits: As early as the 28th week of pregnancy (immediately after birth for deliveries before 28 weeks); postpartum members at any time

summary: In Connecticut, HUSKY Health covers one manual or electric breast pump every two calendar years with a prescription, starting in the third trimester.
timing_and_limits: Manual and electric pumps (E0602, E0603) can be dispensed before an inpatient admission but not before the third trimester; one breast pump in each two calendar years

summary: In Delaware, Medicaid covers manual and double electric breast pumps with no prior authorization for the first pump, and you can request one up to 60 days before your due date.
timing_and_limits: Manual and double-electric pumps can be requested up to 60 days prior to the anticipated delivery date; double-electric purchases limited to one unit every 36 months per household

summary: In DC, Medicaid covers breast pumps as medical equipment, and MedStar Family Choice covers a manual or double electric pump for any breastfeeding mother.
In Florida, Medicaid covers an electric breast pump only when a mother is separated from her baby for work, school or a medical reason, and prior authorization is required.
timing_and_limits: Electric pump (E0603): 1 per 5 years; hospital-grade rental (E0604): 3 months max

summary: In Georgia, Medicaid covers breast pumps only for babies with medical conditions or long NICU stays, and refers other requests to WIC.
timing_and_limits: E0603: maximum of one purchase per qualifying baby; E0604: maximum of three months rentals per qualifying baby without prior authorization

summary: In Hawaii, the Med-QUEST health plans we checked cover breast pumps as a pregnancy benefit, by purchase or rental.
In Idaho, Medicaid covers a manual or electric breast pump every three years with a written order and no prior authorization.
timing_and_limits: One manual or electric pump every three years (purchase only); hospital-grade rental up to three months per birth when the infant has a prolonged hospitalization and a qualifying condition

summary: In Illinois, Medicaid covers a manual or electric breast pump once a year with a practitioner's order and no prior approval.
timing_and_limits: One electric pump per year without prior approval (since January 1, 2024); fee schedule limits E0602 and E0603 to one per 365 days

summary: In Indiana, Medicaid covers manual and electric breast pumps with a written order and no prior authorization.
In Iowa, Medicaid covers manual and electric breast pumps with a prescription.
In Kansas, Medicaid covers one manual or electric breast pump a year with a prescription and no prior authorization.
timing_and_limits: No more than one pump (E0602 and E0603 combined) per year; members ages 12 through 55

summary: In Kentucky, Medicaid covers manual and electric breast pumps, one per calendar year without prior authorization.
timing_and_limits: Electric pump within six weeks before or after birth, up to one replacement per child (907 KAR 1:479); fee schedule limits E0602 and E0603 to one per calendar year without PA

summary: In Louisiana, Medicaid covers a double electric breast pump from 32 weeks of pregnancy with a prescription and no prior authorization.
timing_and_limits: May be obtained from 32 weeks gestational age; Medicaid must not have bought a pump for the same delivery in the past three years

summary: In Maine, MaineCare covers electric breast pumps and supplies with a prescription and no prior authorization or limit.
In Maryland, fee-for-service Medicaid covers manual and electric pumps with a prescription, but HealthChoice plans have to cover them only for listed medical reasons.
timing_and_limits: Fee-for-service: 1 per 3 years (manual and electric). HealthChoice MCOs must cover a pump during the infant's first month of life when a listed medical-necessity condition applies.

summary: In Massachusetts, MassHealth covers one manual or electric breast pump per pregnancy with a prescription.
timing_and_limits: 1 per pregnancy (manual and electric); hospital-grade pump billed as a 1-month rental

summary: In Michigan, Medicaid covers a double electric breast pump every five years or a manual pump each birth, with a practitioner's order and no prior authorization.
timing_and_limits: Personal use double electric: once per five years; manual: once per birth; hospital-grade rental only for a NICU infant up to three months of age, with PA beyond three months

summary: In Minnesota, Medical Assistance lists breast pumps among covered services for pregnant members.
In Mississippi, Medicaid covers breast pumps only when they're medically necessary and prior authorized.
In Missouri, MO HealthNet covers one manual or electric breast pump per lifetime, from the third trimester, with a prescription and no prior authorization.
timing_and_limits: Third trimester of pregnancy; purchase only; one manual or one electric pump per lifetime; WIC services should be exhausted before billing MO HealthNet

summary: In Montana, Medicaid covers a double electric breast pump through its contracted supplier, Aeroflow, from 28 weeks of pregnancy with a prescription.
timing_and_limits: At least 28 weeks gestation or currently breastfeeding; one pump per pregnancy and no more than one per year

summary: In Nebraska, Medicaid covers breast pump rentals only for listed medical conditions, though Nebraska Total Care covers one electric pump per delivery.
timing_and_limits: Fee-for-service rule: short-term rental up to 2 months or long-term rental up to 6 months plus one 6-month extension when a listed condition applies; Nebraska Total Care: one electric pump per delivery, requested during pregnancy until one year after birth

summary: In Nevada, Medicaid covers manual and electric breast pumps for mothers of babies up to 12 months old, with a prescription.
timing_and_limits: Nursing mothers with infants up to 12 months of age; purchase 1 unit per 3 years or rental 1 unit per month for 10 months

summary: In New Hampshire, Medicaid covers one manual breast pump per pregnancy with a prescription.
timing_and_limits: One standard manual breast pump per pregnancy

summary: In New Jersey, Medicaid covers one double electric breast pump per birth with no prescription or prior authorization needed.
timing_and_limits: 1 pump per birth event; available any time during pregnancy and throughout the postpartum period for the duration of breastfeeding

summary: In New Mexico, at least one Turquoise Care health plan (BCBSNM) covers breast pumps and replacement supplies with no prior authorization.
In New York, Medicaid covers a manual or standard electric breast pump once every three years with a practitioner's order and supplier authorization.
timing_and_limits: Manual (E0602) and standard electric (E0603) pumps: once every 3 years (frequency code F4 in the July 1, 2026 manual)

summary: In North Carolina, Medicaid covers an electric breast pump only for medical reasons, such as a newborn still in the hospital.
timing_and_limits: 1 per pregnancy (E0603)

summary: In North Dakota, Medicaid covers a manual breast pump each year or an electric pump every three years, with a prescription and no service authorization.
timing_and_limits: One manual breast pump every year, or one electric breast pump every 3 years

summary: In Ohio, Medicaid covers manual and electric breast pumps with a prescription, and hospital-grade rentals with a certificate of medical necessity.
In Oklahoma, SoonerCare doesn't cover breast pumps and refers members to WIC.
In Oregon, the Oregon Health Plan covers one breast pump per pregnancy without prior authorization once a need is determined after birth.
timing_and_limits: One breast pump purchase per pregnancy, provided after a need is determined following birth; hospital-grade rental covered up to three months

summary: In Pennsylvania, Medical Assistance covers electric breast pumps with a prescription and no prior authorization.
timing_and_limits: One pump per calendar year (E0603)

summary: In Rhode Island, Medicaid health plans cover breast pumps with a prescription.
In South Carolina, Medicaid doesn't pay for breast pumps directly, but all five Healthy Connections health plans offer a free pump as an extra benefit.
timing_and_limits: Varies by plan: Absolute Total Care, request from 12 weeks before to 30 days after delivery (90 days for NICU babies), one per calendar year; First Choice, one per pregnancy; Humana, one non-hospital-grade pump every 2 years

summary: In South Dakota, Medicaid covers manual and electric breast pumps from 28 weeks of pregnancy with a practitioner's order and no prior authorization.
timing_and_limits: Covered from 28 weeks gestation or while breastfeeding; one manual pump per year per family or one electric pump per family every 3 years; hospital-grade rental covered for 1 month, PA needed beyond that

summary: In Tennessee, TennCare plans supply double electric breast pumps through in-network medical equipment suppliers, with a prescription.
In Texas, Medicaid covers a manual or electric breast pump within 12 months of birth with no prior authorization.
timing_and_limits: Manual or electric personal-use pump purchase within 12 months from the date of birth without prior authorization; hospital-grade rental for an initial 60 days, then up to three prior-authorized 90-day rentals within 12 months following birth

summary: In Utah, Medicaid covers breast pumps ordered by a doctor for members who are separated from their baby or have other breastfeeding concerns, with no prior authorization.
timing_and_limits: May be purchased before or after birth; electric pump limited to 1 per year

summary: In Vermont, Medicaid covers a double electric breast pump from 60 days before the due date to 120 days after birth, with a prescription.
timing_and_limits: Personal-use double electric pump (purchase only) from 60 days before the projected due date up to 120 days postpartum; one new pump per lactating person

summary: In Virginia, Medicaid covers manual breast pumps without authorization and electric pumps with service authorization, up to the child's first birthday.
timing_and_limits: Up to the child's first birthday; personal electric pump limited to one purchase every three years

summary: In Washington, Apple Health covers one manual or electric breast pump every three years without prior authorization.
timing_and_limits: Manual or electric pump purchase limited to one per client in a three-year period; hospital-grade rental limited to 3 months unless extended with PA

summary: In West Virginia, Medicaid covers manual and electric breast pumps with a written order and no prior authorization.
timing_and_limits: Electric pump (E0603): 1 unit per rolling year; manual pump (E0602): 1 unit per 5 rolling years

summary: In Wisconsin, ForwardHealth covers a manual or electric breast pump from the third trimester, up to one a year, with a prescription and no prior authorization.
timing_and_limits: From the third trimester of pregnancy or after birth; one pump per year of breastfeeding, up to three purchases without prior authorization

summary: In Wyoming, Medicaid covers manual and electric breast pumps from 28 weeks of pregnancy with a prescription.
timing_and_limits: Manual and electric pumps available at 28 weeks of pregnancy or later; some Public Health Nursing offices provide pumps only after the baby is born
